title: Multipartite entanglement hidden in vector-chiral correlations of spin-1/2 chains
abstract: Characterizing entanglement in quantum materials through experimentally accessible observables remains a central challenge. Quantum Fisher information associated with sums of one-site spin operators provides one route by linking entanglement to measurable magnetic response functions. Extending this approach to local composite observables requires new entanglement bounds. Here we establish a rigorous bound for the total nearest-neighbour vector chirality of periodic spin-$1/2$ chains with an even number of sites. The quantum Fisher information per spin cannot exceed $k+1$ for any $k$-producible state, so exceeding this bound certifies entanglement depth of at least $k+1$. Combining infinite density-matrix renormalization group and thermal pure quantum-state calculations, we demonstrate multipartite entanglement encoded in vector-chiral correlations at zero and finite temperatures in an extended $J_1$-$J_2$ XXZ chain. The spin-current coupling between vector chirality and electric polarization offers, in principle, access to this witness through dielectric loss spectroscopy in multiferroic magnets, extending entanglement diagnostics beyond dipolar spin correlations.
summary: This paper develops a method to quantify multipartite entanglement in quantum spin chains by relating it to the Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) of the vector-chiral correlation. By establishing rigorous upper bounds on this QFI, the authors show that exceeding these bounds certifies a specific depth of entanglement. This provides a powerful, experimentally accessible diagnostic tool for quantum materials research.
main_problem: The central challenge is characterizing and measuring multipartite entanglement in quantum materials using only experimentally accessible observables.
main_result: The study demonstrates that multipartite entanglement is encoded in vector-chiral correlations in the $J_1-J_2$ XXZ chain, providing a new diagnostic route via dielectric spectroscopy.
method: The authors establish rigorous bounds on the Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) associated with the total nearest-neighbour vector chirality, combining iDMRG and thermal quantum-state calculations.
model_or_system: The system analyzed is a spin-1/2 chain, specifically an extended $J_1-J_2$ XXZ chain, which is relevant to multiferroic magnets. The Hamiltonian includes nearest-neighbor and next-nearest-neighbor interactions.
key_observables: Vector Chirality ($\kappa_i$), Total Vector Chirality ($K_{tot}$), and the Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) associated with $K_{tot}$.
important_parameters: Temperature ($T$), chain length ($N$), and the entanglement depth parameter ($k$).
main_assumptions: The QFI-based criterion is sufficient but not necessary for multipartite entanglement. The analysis relies on bounding the QFI for $k$-producible states.
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows the rigorous upper bound for the vector-chirality QFI density. Figure 2 illustrates the structure of the chirality-QFI bound using block partitions.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the theoretical bound for the QFI related to vector chirality. It then applies this bound to the $J_1-J_2$ XXZ chain at both zero and finite temperatures, culminating in a comparison with experimental measurement techniques.
why_interesting: This work bridges the gap between abstract entanglement measures and measurable magnetic responses (dielectric loss), which is highly relevant for experimentalists studying quantum materials and strongly correlated systems.

figures.caption: Figure 1. Multipartite-entanglement threshold for the vector- chirality QFI. The plot shows the rigorous k-producible upper bound for the vector-chirality QFI density at N = 100. The green curve shows the finite-size threshold k+1−s(k−s)/N, with N = qk+s, while the red line shows the simplified bound k + 1. QFI densities above the green threshold certify entanglement depth at least k + 1; the grey region is compatible with k-producible states.

Figure 2. Structure of the chirality-QFI bound. a, Even–odd decomposition of the total vector-chirality operator Ktot into Kodd and Keven. Each component is a sum of mutually non-overlapping nearest-neighbour chirality bonds. b, Example of a block partition compatible with a k = 9-producible pure state for N = 18, shown relative to the odd matching. Each coloured region denotes one block in the chosen product decomposition and contains at most k sites; sites belonging to the same block need not be spatially contiguous.
